about: MUTATING — delete ONE cluster object THE TREE ALREADY PROVES IS UNDECLARED, and nothing else (infra/forge/delete-orphan-object.sh). The converge applies infra/cluster/manifests with no --prune, so deleting a manifest removes the DECLARATION and leaves the OBJECT running; until this verb the only way to clear one was a human typing `kubectl -n boss delete svc <name>`, which blocked a gated-green car for nine days (backlog a139d5bb). THE AUTHORITY IS DERIVED, NOT GRANTED — and that is the whole design: there is deliberately NO general `kubectl delete` verb, because 'delete any object by name' hands an agent namespace-wide destruction through an audited door, which is worse than no door (CLAUDE.md: reads and bounded reclaims are mechanical, destructive-by-policy actions are not). Instead the script re-runs, at call time, the ONE definition of what is orphaned — infra/cluster/undeclared-objects.sh, the same computation the orphan lint reports from — and acts only if that computation NAMES the object it was given, using the kind/namespace/name from the derivation's own output rather than from the packet's string. Five bounds, each refusing loudly and by name: the argument's shape (re-checked in the script, not only here); the declaration set must be A COMMIT — a generation of root's own tree (infra/forge/root-tree.sh: gen/<sha> beside root's bare store, root-owned and writable by nobody else), proved against that store byte for byte before the derivation reads it, so every file the derivation reads (the manifests, instances.toml and the renderer's RENDERS line, the gate-runner yaml, the consist worker's job.json) is reviewed content, a rename in progress or a symlink can never be eligible, and the checkout the runner hands its git verbs, which its owner can edit under root, is never read (backlog 1dde630c); the derivation must say undeclared (it refuses a declared object, a namespace the tree does not own, a kind the tree declares nothing of, an excluded kind, an exempt object, a controller-owned object, an object that is not live — and says CANNOT ANSWER, never 'undeclared', when a credential cannot list the pair or a manifest will not parse); the verb's own KIND FLOOR, narrower than the derivation's scope (Service, ConfigMap, Deployment, CronJob, Job — kinds a manifest reapply restores completely; PVC/StatefulSet are bytes, Secret and ServiceAccount are credentials, Role/RoleBinding are privileges, and all of those stay a named human step); and CAPTURE BEFORE DELETE — the object's YAML is printed onto this packet first, because a deleted object cannot be read back. `--dry-run` runs every bound and deletes nothing, so the verb is exercisable through the runner without acting. Its own timeout: the derivation parses every manifest with kubectl, which exceeds the runner's 30s default. Authorized by David 2026-09-10 ('let's make sure any cars that are blocked on my manual intervention get a job to create an agent-usable mechanism'), same explicit per-verb process as reclaim-disk / rollback-to / converge / publish-github-pr — a precedent for the PROCESS, not a loosened default. GONE IS READ BACK AS NotFound (backlog 1058e686, car B): after the delete the object is read again, and only the server's NotFound prints OK; a get that still finds it is STILL THERE, and any other failure — a timeout, an auth error, an unreachable API server, which the read-back used to count as gone — is CANNOT ANSWER — deleted, not proven gone, exit 1.
effect: ^delete-orphan-object: (OK — [A-Za-z0-9]+ .+ is gone from .+ [(]read back: NotFound[)], and no manifest declared it|DRY RUN — would delete [A-Za-z0-9]+ .+ in .+[.] Every bound passed; nothing was deleted)
